bear_case: NVDA's Stop Day 2 trigger is the bear case's strongest data point. The session high was $195.55 — the stop cleared intraday — but the close was $194.97, $0.03 below the mandatory exit threshold. This means NVDA's demand at the most favorable macro backdrop in weeks (SCOTUS + AI re-rating + Iran stand-down + Dow record) was insufficient to sustain a $195 close. The #1 Russell Growth constituent and AI hardware bellwether could not hold $195 on what may be 2026's strongest macro day — confirming active institutional selling above $195 has now absorbed three consecutive positive catalysts (reconstitution $334B June 26, Samsung Blue House $648B June 29, SCOTUS/AI re-rating June 29). SPX at 7,436 is 24 points below the 7,460 regime floor after this strongest session in weeks; if three simultaneous tailwinds cannot close the gate, a strong NFP (>150K, wages +0.4%) on July 2 locks in the BofA three-hike framework over a 3-day holiday gap — and July 7 opens gap-down into an earnings season with compressed multiples. Invalidation: SPX closes above 7,460 AND VIX closes below 17 simultaneously on June 30 (Q2 close) — regime formally clears and HOLD upgrade is validated. NFP July 2 Goldilocks (90–150K, wages +0.2%) AND SPX sustains above 7,460 on July 7 — BUY upgrade viable for the first time since early June.
